GM collaborates with American motorsport organization [[TWG Motorsports]] through the latter's British subsidiary, '''TWG Cadillac Formula 1 Team Limited'''. Cadillac became the first new, independent constructor to join the grid since [[Haas F1 Team|Haas]] in {{F1|2016}}. The project has three bases in the United States—in [[Fishers, Indiana]]; [[Concord, North Carolina]]; and [[Warren, Michigan]]—as well as a British base in [[Silverstone]]. === Establishment (2023–present) === In January 2023, [[General Motors]] (GM) and the [[Michael Andretti]]-led [[Andretti Global]] announced their intention to enter GM's [[Cadillac]] brand into the [[Formula One World Championship]].{{cite web|url=https://news.cadillac.com/newsroom.detail.html/Pages/news/us/en/2023/jan/0105-andretti.html|title=Andretti Global and General Motors Team Up in F1 Pursuit|date=January 5, 2023|access-date=November 25, 2024|website=[[Cadillac]]}} The [[FIA]] approved their bid but the [[Formula One Group]] vetoed it,{{cite web|url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/josephwolkin/2023/10/02/andretti-global-clears-fia-approval-to-create-a-formula-1-team/|title=Andretti Global Clears FIA Approval To Create A Formula 1 Team|date=October 2, 2024|access-date=November 25, 2024|website=[[Forbes]]|first=Joseph|last=Wolkin}}{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.co.uk/f1/story/_/id/40233366/andretti-buy-existing-f1-team-join-grid-fia-boss|title=Andretti should buy existing F1 team to join grid - FIA boss|date=May 28, 2024|access-date=November 25, 2024|website=[[ESPN]]}} explaining that it would reconsider its decision if GM agreed to manufacture [[Formula One engines]].{{Cite news |last=Smith |first=Luke |title=General Motors enters the grid: Why F1 changed its tune after rejecting Andretti |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/5948455/2024/11/26/general-motors-f1-formula-one-grid-expansion-andretti/ |access-date=December 10, 2024 |work=The New York Times |date=December 2024 |issn=0362-4331}} Following the rejection, Andretti continued to build up the team and operations using [[Toyota Gazoo Racing Europe|Toyota]]'s wind tunnel in [[Cologne]], which [[McLaren]] had recently vacated.{{Cite web |title=Inside McLaren's state-of-the-art new wind tunnel |url=https://www.mclaren.com/racing/formula-1/2023/inside-mclarens-state-of-the-art-new-wind-tunnel/ |access-date=March 20, 2025 |website=www.mclaren.com |language=en-GB}} In November 2024, following extended disputes between the Formula One Group and Michael Andretti,{{Cite web |last=Lawrence |first=Dan |date=February 9, 2025 |title=Michael Andretti realised he was the 'obstacle' to Cadillac F1 bid |url=https://www.motorsportweek.com/2025/02/09/michael-andretti-realised-he-was-the-obstacle-to-cadillac-f1-bid/ |access-date=March 20, 2025 |website=Motorsport Week |language=en-GB}} Andretti Global sponsor [[TWG Global]]—led by [[Mark Walter]]—announced that it was taking over the business operation in areas such as sponsorship, infrastructure planning, and organizational growth.{{Cite web |last=Brown |first=Nathan |title=Andretti Global parent company unveils longtime NASCAR executives as new leaders |url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/motor/2024/12/04/indycar-formula-1-andretti-global-new-leadership-doug-duchardt-jill-gregory/76766459007/ |access-date=December 10, 2024 |website=The Indianapolis Star}}{{Cite web |last=Suttill |first=Josh |date=November 25, 2024 |title=GM, Cadillac agree deal for new 2026 F1 entry - Andretti absent |url=https://www.the-race.com/formula-1/gm-cadillac-2026-f1-team-andretti-absent/ |access-date=December 10, 2024 |website=The Race}}{{Cite web |title=Why Cadillac Deserves to Be in F1 {{!}} FanAmp Insider |url=https://www.fanamp.com/articles/cadillac-f1-2025-fanamp-insider |access-date=December 6, 2025 |website=www.fanamp.com |language=en}} Michael Andretti remained as an advisor, while his father, [[Mario Andretti|Mario]], agreed to serve on the board of directors.{{cite web |date=November 25, 2024 |title=General Motors launches Cadillac Formula 1 Team and power unit |url=https://news.gm.com/home.detail.html/Pages/news/us/en/2024/nov/1125-f1.html |access-date=November 25, 2024 |website=[[General Motors]]}} The team renamed its British subsidiary from ''Andretti Racing'' to ''Cadillac'', and eventually ''TWG Cadillac Formula 1 Team Ltd''.{{Cite web |date=June 24, 2022 |title=TWG Cadillac Formula 1 Team Limited overview - Find and update company information - Gov.uk |url=https://find-and-update.company-information.service.gov.uk/company/14194212 |access-date=January 3, 2026 |website=[[Companies House]] |language=en}} That month, the Formula One Group tentatively approved Cadillac as a new constructor for the {{F1|2026}} season.{{Cite web |date=March 2, 2025 |title=Michael Andretti enjoying retirement as he takes in IndyCar opener as a fan instead of team owner |url=https://apnews.com/article/michael-andretti-indycar-towriss-fa43ed71ceb90fb63a61ccad91a741e9 |access-date=March 20, 2025 |website=AP News |language=en}} The entry received its final approval in March 2025,{{Cite news |date=March 9, 2025 |title=Caddy back |work=[[The Sunday Times (Western Australia)|The Sunday Times]] |department=Sport |publisher=[[Seven West Media]] |location=Perth |page=48 |language=en-au |issn=1442-9527 |oclc=427972890}} in time for Cadillac to sign the latest [[Concorde Agreement]].{{Cite news |last=Horton |first=Phillip |date=March 18, 2025 |title=Cadillac Will Pay $450 Million Anti-Dilution Fee to Join Formula 1 |url=https://www.autoweek.com/racing/formula-1/a64218356/cadillac-will-pay-450-million-anti-dilution-fee-join-formula-1/ |access-date=March 20, 2025 |work=Autoweek}} The approval by the FIA and Formula One Management confirmed Cadillac's place on the grid as the championship's 11th team for the 2026 season.{{Cite web |title=Cadillac receive final approval to join F1 grid in 2026 |url=https://www.formula1.com/en/latest/article/cadillac-receive-final-approval-to-join-formula-1-grid-in-2026-as-11th-team.1saxQLtLPc7k9TFl4eNrQN |access-date=February 11, 2026 |website=www.formula1.com |language=en}}{{Cite web |last=Baldwin |first=Alan |date=March 8, 2025 |title=GM-backed Cadillac F1 team confirmed for 2026 |url=https://www.reuters.com/sports/formula1/f1-fia-approve-gm-backed-cadillac-entry-2026-2025-03-07/}} Cadillac will be the first debutant Formula One venture since [[Haas F1 Team|Haas]] in {{F1|2016}}.{{cite news |last1=Coleman |first1=Madeline |date=November 25, 2024 |title=Formula 1 expands grid as General Motors to become the 11th team in 2026 |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/5947118/2024/11/25/formula-1-expands-grid-general-motors/ |access-date=December 16, 2024 |work=The New York Times}} GM paid an expansion fee of {{currency|450|USD}} million, over twice as much as originally demanded.{{Cite web |last=Collantine |first=Keith |date=January 17, 2025 |title=$450 million payment for Cadillac to join Formula 1 is too low - Wolff |url=https://www.racefans.net/2025/01/17/450-million-payment-for-cadillac-to-join-formula-1-is-too-low-wolff/ |access-date=January 17, 2025 |website=RaceFans |language=en-GB}} In addition, GM announced that it would begin manufacturing engines for Cadillac for the 2029 season;{{cite web |date=November 25, 2024 |title=Statement on General Motors application to join FIA Formula One World Championship in 2026 |url=https://www.formula1.com/en/latest/article/statement-on-general-motors-application-to-join-fia-formula-one-world.69uoRF1uwHwXkr4efkpnhc |access-date=November 25, 2024 |website=[[Formula 1]]}} until then, the team will compete with [[Scuderia Ferrari|Ferrari]] engines. In November, Cadillac made its testing debut at [[Imola Circuit|Imola]] with [[Sergio Pérez]] driving a blank-liveried [[Ferrari SF-23]].{{Cite web |url=https://www.autosport.com/f1/news/exclusive-first-image-as-sergio-perez-and-cadillac-test-ferrari-f1-car-at-imola/10776317 |title=Exclusive: Pérez and Cadillac test Ferrari F1 car at Imola |last1=Cleeren |first1=Filip |last2=Rava |first2=Jacopo |date=November 13, 2025 |website=[[Autosport]] |publisher=[[Motorsport Network]] |access-date=November 13, 2025 |issn=0269-946X |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251113154046/https://www.autosport.com/f1/news/exclusive-first-image-as-sergio-perez-and-cadillac-test-ferrari-f1-car-at-imola/10776317/ |archive-date=November 13, 2025 |url-status=live}} The project has been described as part of an effort to expand American involvement in top-tier motorsport. |url-status=live}} == Power unit program == GM and TWG established '''GM Performance Power Units LLC''' (GM PPU) to produce [[works team|works]] engines for the Cadillac team, and hired longtime GM engine designer Russ O'Blenes to lead the engine division. In addition, [[Joe Saward]] reported that GM was seeking to purchase the intellectual property of Renault's former power unit program.{{Cite web |last=Lawrence |first=Dan |date=October 24, 2024 |title=Cadillac circling Renault F1 engine IP – report |url=https://www.motorsportweek.com/2024/10/24/cadillac-circling-renault-f1-engine-ip-report/ |access-date=December 10, 2024 |website=Motorsport Week}} GM PPU plans to produce [[Formula One power units]] for the 2029 season, using [[Scuderia Ferrari|Ferrari]] power units and gearboxes until then.{{Cite news |date=April 23, 2025 |title=Cadillac F1 team: FIA approves General Motors as new Formula 1 engine supplier from 2029 |url=https://www.skysports.com/f1/news/12433/13354351/cadillac-f1-team-fia-approves-general-motors-as-new-formula-1-engine-supplier-from-2029 |access-date=April 23, 2025 |work=Sky Sports}}{{Cite web |title=Ferrari enters a multi-year agreement with Andretti Formula Racing|url=https://www.ferrari.com/en-EN/corporate/articles/ferrari-enters-a-multi-year-agreement-with-andretti-formula-racing |access-date=December 10, 2024 |website=[[Ferrari]]}}{{Cite web |title=Cadillac provide update on in-house engine schedule |url=https://www.formula1.com/en/latest/article/cadillac-provide-update-on-when-in-house-f1-engine-might-make-debut.3Req6t80EL5bi3i8TYErEG |access-date=2026-04-14 |website=www.formula1.com |language=en}} GM PPU announced that it plans to spend {{currency|65|USD}}–70 million building an engine factory for 300–350 employees, which is expected to open in the first quarter of 2027, and an additional US$75–80 million in start-up fees.{{Cite web |last=Noble |first=Jon |date=February 11, 2025 |title=Cadillac F1's plan for new $150m factory revealed |url=https://www.the-race.com/formula-1/cadillac-f1-plan-new-150m-us-based-factory-revealed/ |access-date=February 14, 2025 |website=The Race |language=en}} The power unit program is managed by GM Performance Power Units LLC (GM PPU), a dedicated subsidiary established to develop Formula One's next-generation hybrid powertrains. In February 2025, the City of Concord approved a US$150 million project to construct a 204,045-square-foot facility at 4295 Defender Way, adjacent to the Hendrick Motorsports campus.{{cite news |date=2025-02-13 |title=City of Concord unanimously approves F1 team's engine facility project |url=https://www.wsoctv.com/news/local/city-concord-unanimously-approves-f1-teams-engine-facility-project/K6R25JEGXNBLXIHLKNSX5MN7JQ/ |access-date=2026-03-18 |publisher=WSOC-TV}} The facility, which involves a US$70 million construction cost and an additional US$80 million investment in state-of-the-art dynamometers and R&D equipment, is expected to be fully operational by the first quarter of 2027.{{cite news |last=Taylor |first=S. |date=2025-02-11 |title=Cadillac ramping up plans to build $150m F1 engine facility |url=https://www.motorsportweek.com/2025/02/11/cadillac-ramping-up-plans-to-build-150m-f1-engine-facility/ |access-date=2026-03-18 |publisher=Motorsport Week}} Until the permanent site is completed, GM PPU is conducting preliminary testing and engineering at an interim facility located at 4540 Fortune Way NW in Concord.{{cite web |last=Plotnick |first=B. |date=2025-02-14 |title=Cadillac F1 Team to Create 350 Jobs with $85M Concord Project |url=https://power98fm.com/2025/02/14/cadillac-f1-team-to-create-350-jobs-with-85m-concord-project-plans-2025-factory-launch/ |access-date=2026-03-18 |website=Power 98 FM}} == Facilities == [[File:Interstate Highway 69 winds its way north through the Indianapolis suburb of Fishers, Indiana.jpg|thumb|right|Cadillac will be headquartered at a purpose-built facility in [[Fishers, Indiana]].|alt=Aerial view of a highway passing through Fishers, Indiana]] Cadillac plans to operate four facilities, in: [[Fishers, Indiana]]; [[Concord, North Carolina]]; [[Warren, Michigan]]; and [[Northamptonshire]], England. The organization will be headquartered at a brand-new facility in Fishers—a suburb of [[Indianapolis]]—which will handle "the bulk" of manufacturing.{{Cite news |last=Brown |first=Nathan |date=March 12, 2025 |title='This is an American team': Cadillac F1 will build cars in Fishers headquarters |url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/motor/2025/03/12/cadillac-f1-new-headquarters-fishers-indiana-build-cars-american-team/82311732007/ |access-date=March 18, 2025 |work=The Indianapolis Star}} In January 2026, team principal Graeme Lowdon stated that the organization had advertised 595 positions, receiving 143,265 applications, and had hired 520 staff by the end of 2025.{{Cite web |last=Baldwin |first=Alan |date=January 25, 2026 |title=Off track, the numbers are adding up for F1 newcomers Cadillac |url=https://www.reuters.com/sports/formula1/off-track-numbers-are-adding-up-f1-newcomers-cadillac-2026-01-25/}} Andretti Global initially suggested that it would base its Formula One and IndyCar operations in same building,{{Cite news |last=Cooper |first=Adam |date=January 31, 2024 |title=Andretti's plan to run an F1 team from four locations |url=https://www.motorsport.com/f1/news/andrettis-plan-run-f1-team-four-locations/10570962/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240204002433/https://www.motorsport.com/f1/news/andrettis-plan-run-f1-team-four-locations/10570962/ |archive-date=February 4, 2024 |access-date=December 19, 2024 |work=Motorsport.com |language=en |url-status=live }} but the IndyCar operation was ultimately moved to a different facility; [[Formula One regulations]] prohibit the use of multi-team facilities.{{Cite web |last=Brown |first=Nathan |title=Andretti Global seeking additional racing shop following F1 admission, sources say |url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/motor/2025/01/29/andretti-global-seeking-another-indy-area-race-shop-alongside-fishers-indycar-formula-imsa-f1/78002005007/ |access-date=January 29, 2025 |website=The Indianapolis Star |language=en-US}} GM will build a 204,000-square foot power unit facility near its [[Charlotte, North Carolina|Charlotte]] Technical Center in Concord.{{Cite web |date=January 9, 2025 |title=TWG Motorsports and GM name Russ O'Blenes to lead Cadillac Formula 1 power units venture |url=https://news.gm.com/home.detail.html/Pages/news/us/en/2025/jan/0109-twg.html |access-date=January 11, 2025 |website=General Motors}} Additional operations will take place in Warren—the location of the [[General Motors Technical Center]]. In addition, the team has signed a long-term agreement with [[Toyota Gazoo Racing Europe|Toyota]] to rent their [[wind tunnel]] in [[Cologne]], Germany.{{Cite web |last=Brittle |first=Cian |date=March 11, 2025 |title=Cadillac team principal: Commercial interest 'outstripping capacity' ahead of F1 debut |url=https://www.blackbookmotorsport.com/news/cadillac-f1-graeme-lowdon-sponsor-interest-general-motors-march-2025/ |access-date=March 20, 2025 |website=BlackBook Motorsport |language=en-GB}} The race team, competing under an [[List of Formula One constructors#Team's nationality|American racing licence]],{{cite web|title=Cadillac|url=https://www.statsf1.com/en/cadillac.aspx|publisher=StatsF1|access-date=January 14, 2026}} and chassis designers will operate from a facility in [[Silverstone]], England.{{Cite web |last=Moat |first=David |date=April 10, 2024 |title=Andretti Global Opens New Facility at Silverstone |url=https://andrettiglobal.com/news/2024/04/andretti-global-opens-new-facility-at-silverstone/ |access-date=March 20, 2025 |website=Andretti Global |language=en-US}} The Fishers campus represents a US$200 million investment and serves as the primary hub for chassis manufacturing and research and development.{{cite news |date=2025-03-18 |title=Cadillac F1 team plans to employ 300 people at new HQ in Fishers |url=https://www.insideindianabusiness.com/articles/cadillac-f1-team-plans-to-employ-300-people-at-new-hq-in-fishers |access-date=2026-03-18 |publisher=Inside Indiana Business}} While originally intended as a universal headquarters for all Andretti Global programs, the 400,000-square-foot facility was repurposed for exclusive Formula One use to comply with FIA regulations prohibiting the co-location of multiple racing series to prevent cost-cap circumvention.{{cite web |date=2025-03-17 |title=Formula One Facility Coming to Fishers Soon |url=https://www.larryinfishers.com/2025/03/17/formula-one-facility-coming-to-fishers/ |access-date=2026-03-18 |website=LarryInFishers.com}}{{cite news |last=Cipolloni |first=Mark |date=2025-02-03 |title=Andretti barred from co-locating all their teams in massive Fishers, IN. facility |url=https://www.autoracing1.com/pl/444234/andretti-barred-from-co-locating-all-their-teams-in-massive-fishers-in-facility/ |access-date=2026-03-18 |publisher=AutoRacing1}} Consequently, non-F1 operations, including IndyCar and Formula E, were relocated to a separate 240,000-square-foot facility in Indianapolis.{{cite news |date=2025-03-04 |title=Andretti Global confirms move of IndyCar and Formula E into new facility |url=https://www.motorsport.com/indycar/news/andretti-global-confirms-move-of-indycar-and-formula-e-into-new-facility/10700269/ |access-date=2026-03-18
